22151-a-treatise-of-the-cohabitacyon-of-:
A Treatise of the Cohabitacyon of the Faithfull with the Unfaithfull argues a hard question of the Reformation age. Should true Christians keep company with those they judge ungodly? The text, printed in the old spelling, leans on Paul's letters. Paul wrote that believers should not company with fornicators. Yet they could not shun all sinners of this world, or they must needs go out of the world.

The treatise works through that distinction for a church under pressure. Its archaic type and spelling mark it as a survivor of the earliest English Protestant press. Such tracts shaped Separatist and Puritan thought about pure churches. It is a brief, fierce piece of Tudor religious argument.
doe-osti-3008309-single-walled-carbon-na:
Platinum-free fuel cell catalysts are covered in the final report for DOE award DE-EE0010432 from the University of California, Riverside. Principal investigator Juchen Guo worked with Bryan Wong on catalysts made from single-walled carbon nanotubes holding confined chalcogens. The project ran from June 2023 to May 2025.

The target reaction is oxygen reduction at the fuel cell cathode, where platinum's cost blocks wide deployment. Sulfur-filled nanotubes first looked active, but careful controls traced the activity to an iron sulfide impurity rather than the nanotubes themselves. Pure sulfur-filled samples showed no activity. Calculations explained the miss: oxygen barely transfers electrons to the sulfur-filled tubes, so the reaction stalls at its first step.
doe-osti-3013601-a-case-study-in-contras:
Pacific Northwest National Laboratory's November 2025 case study applies contrastive learning to a forensic problem. The authors are Alex Hagen, Charlie Hayden, Cody Nizinski, Cuong Ly, and Jessie Yaros. The problem is identifying which filament source produced a 3D-printed part. Different measurement types describe the same object in different languages. Investigators need those views combined into one identification.

The study tests methods for combining information, drawn from machine learning. They include attention-based models. In those models, the mixing of inputs shifts with the data itself. The authors argue that this dynamic weighting fits technical forensics well. The model can focus on relevant signals and ignore irrelevant ones. One modality can also give context to another. The filament case is the worked example. It supports a general framework for multi-instrument identification problems.
doe-osti-3683725-verification-and-valida:
Sandia report SAND2026-25542 checks a flow confinement model inside the OpenFAST turbine simulator. Dongyoung Kim and Vincent S. Neary of Sandia wrote it with Emmanuel Branlard of the University of Massachusetts Amherst. Wind and water turbines tested in tunnels feel the tunnel walls, which squeeze the flow. OpenFAST's source panel method models that squeeze so test data and free-flow runs can be compared fairly. The base method came from earlier open-source work.

The report first lays out the panel maths, the no-flow-through wall rule, and a global mass saving fix. Checks then test grid, time step, and wall panel spacing for steady answers. A model turbine case from a past tunnel study serves for validation. Acceptance rules state in advance how close model and test must sit.
doe-osti-3874827-relaxing-topological-co:
Los Alamos report LA-UR-26-28098, issued September 10, 2026, loosens a strict rule in quadrilateral mesh refinement. Caden Fischer and Hannah Shaw are the printed authors, advised by Jacob Jones, Jonathan Woodring, and Konstantin Lipnikov. Fluid simulations need meshes of four-sided cells that split evenly as they refine. The lab's meshing code, Crosslink, long required matching split counts on opposite sides of each block. That equality rule blocks many shapes engineers actually need to mesh.

Two new algorithms drop the rule in unlike ways. Both trim the busiest sides step by step, keeping opposite counts close. A ring of plain square pads around the edge then smooths the corners. Tests against published methods show better cell quality scores. The report is dated June 2026 and reads as a student project write-up. Its methods widen the shapes Crosslink can refine without hand fixes.
